state.required: Implement true per-Calendar SQLite Durable Object authority. Children inherit it; root IDs derive complete app/team/principal/operation/opID identity. Every mutation one owner; reject cross-root reads/writes; use fresh Identity D1 auth facts without claiming distributed atomic auth. Directory D1 eventual discovery only, direct routed IDs work before indexing. Must implement now; no D1 business fallback.
verified: DESIGN section7 specifies per-root DO authority, routable child references, eventual directory, and one-authority fences/receipts/outbox.
Current canonical invoker accepts StoragePort and fresh ResolvedIdentity, performs State admission/receipts/commit; native create IDs use operationId#create:index and require new allocator hook.
createDOStorage + ensureSchema is real SQLite StoragePort. Existing DO class is TEST-ONLY arbitrary method RPC and cannot be production reused.
Current worker uses D1 business store and supports team D1 routing. No existing production DO root routing or directory.
Record references use opaque string IDs; root prefix in IDs avoids adding user-settable authority fields. Must still verify Values/ID length behavior.

Whole-invocation actor can receive original credential-bearing HTTP request, independently authenticate using Identity D1 and execute canonical invocation with local DO StoragePort. Requires trusted store/allocator composition hooks and concrete generated class export.

Alternative scoped StoragePort protocol keeps canonical invoker on frontend and forwards fixed validated load/query/commit/receipt actions to DO with signed fresh scope and bound actor. It still uses local atomic commit and optimistic fence, but business reads/evaluation cross RPC and replay/authority/session capabilities need transport-safe handling.

Either design must pin root/team, reject foreign mutable records, preserve evaluation order and atomic commit/outbox, provide actual emitted-source tests, and implement eventual directory separately with owner-written work.

boundary.instructions: Which implementation boundary best meets per-root authority, recovery and maintainability given these existing producer APIs?

criteria.actor: Route each business request to its root actor, reauthenticate there, and use existing canonical evaluation/receipts with direct DO storage. Expose no arbitrary storage RPC.
criteria.port: Reuse frontend evaluation by transporting a complete allowlisted StoragePort to its root DO. Authenticate scope and maintain all fence and session provenance semantics across calls.
